item.title: 21 dead, 541 missing after mudslide hits border port in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Twenty-one people have been confirmed dead and 541 others remain missing as of Wednesday noon after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, according to the regional government's latest news briefing.
Rescuers have recovered 847 pieces of personal belongings, according to the news briefing. Local authorities have received 876 phone calls from the relatives of the victims and missing people, and have been promptly replying to their requests.
Caused by an ice-rock avalanche in Nepal, the deadly mudslide swept through the area and destroyed buildings, power supplies and a section of the G216 highway leading to Gyirong Port, which seriously hampered emergency response and rescue efforts.
Despite such difficulties, China has immediately mobilized helicopters, speedboats and rubber rafts to carry rescuers to the mudslide-hit port. Ground rescue teams have spent 12 hours traversing the steep mountain roads and reached the area on foot.
To date, some 2,300 rescue personnel, more than 400 search-and-rescue vehicles, over 8,000 sets of professional equipment, over 800 drone flights and 24 helicopter flights have been deployed. A total of 5.43 tonnes of materials and equipment have been airdropped to the area.
Telecom operators have restored 12 base stations in the port area, ensuring communications for emergency command, rescue operations and supply coordination.
At the core affected zone, some 336 rescuers have conducted multiple rounds of thorough and exhaustive search and rescue operations, covering a cumulative area of 1.591 million square meters.
Road access to the zone was basically restored at 10 a.m. Wednesday after days of round-the-clock repair work on the G216. Over 10 pieces of heavy machinery have entered the core area to aid on-site rescuers.
Ren Wei, executive vice chairman of the Xizang people's government, told the media briefing that after the road access was restored, rescuers will conduct more thorough searches using professional instruments and equipment, and do their utmost to locate those missing. Priority searches will also be carried out at key sites for the parking lots, as well as the joint‑inspection and dormitory buildings.
Ren said rescuers are using radars and other equipment to monitor the surrounding environment around the clock to guard against secondary disasters, while meteorological authorities are providing weather forecasts every six hours.
Debris‑flow deposits in the core disaster area are an average of four meters thick, reaching up to 16 meters at their deepest, with a significant amount of large rocks and silt covering the surface.
Tan Xiangdong, Party chief of the Xizang regional health commission, said at the media briefing that professional teams have been dispatched to provide psychological assistance to families of the dead and missing, as well as mental‑health support to rescuers.
Chen Fuqi, chief engineer of the Xizang regional department of natural resources, said regional authorities will conduct extensive hazard screening in the plateau canyon, establish an integrated air‑space‑ground monitoring system, and improve multi‑agency coordination, as well as cross‑border disaster early‑warning and information‑sharing mechanisms to boost emergency response capacity.

item.title: China willing to support more visits, exchanges between Chinese, U.S. people: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- China will support more visits and exchanges between the peoples of China and the United States as always, so that the two countries can continue to write new chapters in their people-to-people friendship and make greater contributions to the development of bilateral relations, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said Wednesday.
Spokesperson Guo Jiakun told a daily news briefing that recently, Ronald Sakolsky, affectionately known in China as "Saikaosi" for supporting China's fight against desertification, visited China upon invitation after 27 years.
During his visit, Sakolsky traveled to Inner Mongolia, where he joined the national model worker Yin Yuzhen, according to Guo. Sakolsky revisited the forest he helped fund years ago and planted a tree of friendship with Yin together. He also returned to the school in Luoyang, Henan Province, where he once taught, to meet with teachers and students, and visited Beijing as well.
Guo pointed out that throughout his visit, Sakolsky witnessed firsthand the remarkable changes that have taken place in China and once again experienced the warmth and hospitality of the Chinese people, and he was deeply moved and shed tears on several occasions.
In an interview with the media, Sakolsky said that Yin and he have shown that they can bridge cultures and break down boundaries, adding that the U.S. and Chinese people both want to live in peace. The two countries are like two roads -- they may take different routes, but they can still lead to the same destination, Sakolsky said.
"His sincere words have touched many people, reflecting a shared aspiration of the people of both countries," Guo said.
The hope of the China-U.S. relationship lies in the people, and its foundation lies in grassroots connections, Guo said, adding that many inspiring stories written together by the Chinese and U.S. people are a vivid testament to the people-to-people friendship.
"They also once again demonstrate that China and the United States, as two major countries, can achieve mutual success and contribute to the well-being of the world," he added.

item.title: Xi's special envoy attends Zambian president's inauguration
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Zambian President Hakainde Hichilema delivers a speech during his swearing-in ceremony at the National Heroes Stadium in Lusaka, September 1, 2026. /Xinhua
Chinese President Xi Jinping's Special Envoy Xian Hui attended the inauguration of President Hakainde Hichilema of Zambia in Lusaka on Tuesday, at the invitation of the Zambian government.
Hichilema met with Xian, who is also the vice chairperson of the National Committee of the Chinese People's Political Consultative Conference, at the Community House on Wednesday.
Xian conveyed Xi's cordial greetings and best wishes to Hichilema, noting that China is willing to work with Zambia, guided by the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, to carry forward the traditional friendship, deepen political mutual trust and practical cooperation, firmly support each other, strengthen international coordination, and push for greater development of the China-Zambia comprehensive strategic cooperative partnership to better benefit the two peoples.
For his part, Hichilema asked Xian to convey his sincere greetings to Xi and expressed gratitude to Xi for sending a special envoy to attend his inauguration ceremony.
Noting that Zambia is grateful to China for its long-standing and valuable support, Hichilema said that the Zambian side will continue to firmly abide by the one-China principle and actively expand friendly and mutually beneficial cooperation with China in various fields, including new energy, the digital economy, and artificial intelligence.

item.title: Xi returns to Beijing after SCO summit, state visits to Kyrgyzstan, Egypt
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
BEIJING, Sept. 3 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping returned to Beijing on Thursday after attending the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit 2026 in Bishkek, and concluding his state visits to Kyrgyzstan and Egypt.
Xi's entourage, including his wife Peng Liyuan, Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and director of the General Office of the CPC Central Committee, and Wang Yi, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Chinese foreign minister, returned on the same flight.

item.title: China's Xinjiang accelerates green, smart energy transition
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
An aerial drone photo shows an all-vanadium redox flow energy storage integrated project of China Three Gorges Corporation (CTG) in Jimsar, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Aug. 30, 2026. (Photo by He Long/Xinhua)
KARAMAY, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- In 2026, the first year of China's 15th Five-Year Plan period, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region has remained firmly committed to its strategic roles and accelerated the transition toward greener, smarter and more effective energy development and utilization.
In the oil and gas sector, a series of key core technologies have seen major breakthroughs, achieving economically viable development of unconventional oil and gas resources while significantly raising single-well productivity. Meanwhile, more new energy projects combining photovoltaic power generation with long-duration energy storage help provide clean energy to tens of thousands of households. Digital and intelligent technologies have been applied across the entire process of energy exploitation, development and production.
Xinjiang is tapping its resource advantages while enabling innovation to play a greater role in a continuing endeavor to lay a solid foundation for a modern industrial system.
Staff members inspect a pilot facility for carbon dioxide miscible flooding at Xinjiang Oilfield Company of China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) in Karamay, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Sept. 1, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Lei)
Staff members do patrol checking at a shale oil joint station of Jiqing Oilfield operation area of Xinjiang Oilfield Company of China National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) in Jimsar, northwest China's Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, Aug. 30, 2026. (Xinhua/Ding Lei)

item.title: Road access to Gyirong Port cleared, rescuers carry on comprehensive, in-depth search across affected area
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Excavators and other heavy machinery work to repair a water-damaged section of National Highway G216, Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, August 31, 2026. /VCG
Road access to the core area of Gyirong Port was basically restored at 10 a.m. on Wednesday, enabling rescue teams to adjust their deployment and comprehensively improve the efficiency of search operations in the mudslide-hit Gyirong County, southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region, according to China's Ministry of Emergency Management.
Since the disaster occurred, roads across the valley have been extensively damaged, with landslides, rocks and mud blocking access in multiple areas. During the initial stage of the rescue operation, rescue task forces conducted preliminary grid searches in the core area of the port mainly by moving on foot, using drones for reconnaissance and airlifting lightweight equipment.
With the rescue access route restored, rescue teams promptly adjusted their tactics, optimized the deployment of personnel and maximized the effectiveness of rescue operations.
For search operations, a coordinated search-and-rescue approach has been adopted, under which large engineering machinery clears obstacles and opens up working areas, professional rescue teams follow up with targeted searches and life-detection equipment is used.
Rescue teams are closely following the machinery as it clears the way, carrying out meticulous searches of areas with large rock accumulations, sites where buildings have been buried and sediment-filled sections of river channels. Wherever the machinery clears a path, targeted search and rescue operations follow.
Going forward, rescue teams will work in coordination with other rescue forces to carry out comprehensive and in-depth searches across the affected area, leaving no area that may have been overlooked unchecked and making every effort to find survivors.

item.title: Xi, Peng Liyuan visit Grand Egyptian Museum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan, accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi, tour the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Xie Huanchi)
CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife, Peng Liyuan, visited on Wednesday the Grand Egyptian Museum accompanied by Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife.
The two heads of state and their spouses took in the exquisite and imposing stone carvings and inscribed stone pillars. They then gazed out at the pyramids from the museum's observation deck.
Entering the Tutankhamun exhibition hall, the two presidents viewed such prized treasures as the pharaoh's throne, the golden mask and royal chariots.
Noting that China and Egypt are both ancient civilizations and countries rich in World Heritage sites, Xi said that across time and space, the two civilizations have been reaching out to each other, adding new chapters of everlasting friendship between the two peoples.
Xi called on both sides to uphold the vision of civilization based on equality, mutual learning, dialogue and inclusiveness, and implement the Global Civilization Initiative.
He also urged the two countries to promote the inclusive coexistence and mutual learning among different civilizations, and pool greater strength from civilizations to advance the building of a community with a shared future for humanity.
Sisi thanked Xi for extending congratulations on the opening of the museum last year. He said the ancient Egyptian and Chinese civilizations share the qualities of openness, inclusiveness and harmonious coexistence amid diversity, which closely aligns with the vision of the Global Civilization Initiative proposed by Xi.
The Egyptian side stands ready to work with China to step up people-to-people and cultural exchanges, promote mutual learning among civilizations, and make the world more harmonious and inclusive, Sisi said.

item.title: Xi calls for deepening China-Egypt cooperation, raises Mideast proposal
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-03
Chinese President Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan pose for a group photo with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi and his wife Entissar El-Sisi in Cairo, Egypt, Sept. 2, 2026. Xi held talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi in Cairo on Wednesday. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu)
CAIRO, Sept. 2 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Wednesday called on China and Egypt to support each other, deepen cooperation, and continue advancing the building of a China-Egypt community with a shared future amid a turbulent international and regional landscape.
Xi made the remarks during his talks with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi, while emphasizing China's support for regional countries in building a new security architecture in the Middle East via upholding a vision of common, comprehensive, cooperative and sustainable security.
ENHANCING BILATERAL EXCHANGES, COOPERATION
Noting that Egypt was the first Arab and African nation to establish diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China in 1956, Xi said that the older-generation leaders of the two countries led their peoples in striving side by side for national independence and against imperialism and colonialism, forging an unbreakable bond of friendship.
Over the past seven decades, China-Egypt relations have weathered challenges and developed distinctive features of equality and mutual trust, friendship and mutual learning, solidarity and mutual support, as well as win-win cooperation, he said.
Xi said the China-Egypt comprehensive strategic partnership has achieved leapfrog development in recent years under the guidance of the two heads of state. The two sides share similar views and have closely aligned strategies in pursuing development and revitalization, improving people's well-being, and upholding international fairness and justice, he added.
Xi emphasized that China and Egypt should firmly support each other, maintain the momentum of high-level exchanges, enhance exchanges and cooperation in all fields and at all levels, and strengthen exchanges and mutual learning on governance experience.
Xi said the two sides should promote mutually beneficial cooperation, better align their development strategies, tap the potential for cooperation in traditional fields such as infrastructure development, power, agriculture and communications technology, and foster new highlights of cooperation in green energy, electric vehicles, aerospace, the digital economy and modern agricultural technology.
The two sides should promote people-to-people exchanges, comprehensively expand exchanges and cooperation in culture, education, science and technology, health, sports and other fields, and facilitate personnel exchanges and enhance people-to-people bonds, Xi said.
The two sides should strengthen security cooperation, jointly combat transnational crime, deepen international cooperation in anti-corruption, firmly support each other's anti-terror efforts, and safeguard their common security, Xi said.
The two sides should strengthen multilateral collaboration, further enhance coordination and cooperation on multilateral platforms such as the United Nations and the BRICS, jointly promote the development of the China-Arab States Cooperation Forum and the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, jointly oppose unilateralism and acts of bullying, and promote a more just and equitable global governance system, Xi said.
For his part, Sisi welcomed Xi's historic state visit to Egypt on the occasion of the 70th anniversary of diplomatic ties between the two countries.
Sisi said that since the establishment of diplomatic relations, bilateral ties have developed in a sound and steady manner, and cooperation across various fields has yielded fruitful results.
Egypt firmly adheres to the one-China principle and is committed to further advancing the Egypt-China comprehensive strategic partnership, Sisi added.
Egypt is ready to work with China to deepen cooperation in trade and investment, manufacturing, infrastructure development, finance, science and technology, and new energy, strengthen military and security exchanges, and promote closer people-to-people exchanges, so as to benefit the two peoples and contribute to regional development and prosperity, Sisi said.
Sisi said China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, plays an important and constructive role in international affairs. Egypt is ready to strengthen coordination with China at multilateral platforms, jointly address global challenges, and work together to uphold international fairness and justice, he added.
The two heads of state jointly witnessed the signing of multiple cooperation documents on Belt and Road cooperation, artificial intelligence, economic and trade, and industrial and supply chain cooperation.
The two sides also issued a joint statement on further deepening their comprehensive strategic partnership, and signed more than 20 cooperation documents covering such areas as digital economy, science and technology, education, and transportation.
NEW REGIONAL SECURITY ARCHITECTURE
In the talks, Xi raised a four-point proposal on building a new security architecture in the Middle East, saying that China supports countries in the region in developing good-neighborly and friendly relations.
To promote common security in the region, Xi said that efforts should be made to foster the internal driving force for common security in the region.
People in the Middle East should remain masters of their own affairs, and external interference should be rejected, Xi said, noting that China supports regional countries in strengthening dialogue on peace and security, exploring the building of a new security architecture for the Middle East, and taking their future into their own hands.
Xi said that a comprehensive approach should be adopted to advance common security in the region and that given the multiple hotspots in the Middle East and their close interconnections, comprehensive solutions should be pursued.
The Palestinian issue remains at the core of the Middle East question and should never be overlooked or marginalized, he added.
The foundation for common security should be strengthened through development, Xi said, noting that lasting peace and stability in the Middle East fundamentally depend on development.
China stands ready to work with Middle East countries to safeguard the security of international shipping lanes, advance development cooperation, promote the convergence of interests of regional countries, gradually enhance mutual trust, and eliminate the root causes of the conflict, he said.
Xi urged that international coordination for common security in the region should be strengthened, and the UN Charter and international law should serve as the fundamental principles for handling Middle East affairs.
The international community, especially external powers, should abandon double standards in the Middle East, respect the sovereignty and territorial integrity of regional countries, and safeguard regional peace and stability, Xi added.
He also urged support for the United Nations' effective role in Middle East affairs.
Sisi said that Egypt highly appreciates China's consistent, objective, and impartial stance on the Middle East question, noting that Egypt is committed to promoting de-escalation in the region, resolving conflicts and differences through political means, and advancing regional security and development.
Egypt stands ready to continue strengthening coordination with China to ease tensions in the Middle East, safeguard regional stability, and explore a regional security architecture, Sisi said.

item.title: Pushing in by Land, Water and Air: Expert Explains Extreme Hurdles in Mudslide Rescue
item.description:
Published: 2026-08-30
A total of 2,141 rescue personnel have been mobilized for search and rescue operations after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region. Rescue teams are advancing into the hardest-hit core area simultaneously by water, land and air. An expert explained mudslides like this occur under particular terrain and water conditions, and that creates several challenges for rescue teams.
